questions.question: What is meant by reverse saturation current? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • What is meant by reverse saturation current? [K] / [CO1] Ans. Reverse saturation current is the small current that flows in a pn junction under reverse bias due to thermally generated minority carriers. It is almost independent of the applied reverse voltage and depends strongly on temperature and material properties. It is denoted by 𝐼0in the diode equation. Correct definition of reverse saturation current – 2 mark

questions.question: Does the mass action law hold true for degenerate semiconductors? Why? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Does the mass action law hold true for degenerate semiconductors? Why? [U] / [CO1] Ans. No, the mass action law does not hold for degenerate semiconductors. This is because they are heavily doped and the carrier concentrations no longer follow Maxwell–Boltzmann statistics but instead obey Fermi–Dirac statistics. Hence, the relation 𝑛𝑝 = 𝑛𝑖2is no longer valid. Correct statement (does not hold for degenerate semiconductors) – 1 mark Reason– 1 mark

questions.question: How is a p-type semiconductor formed? Explain with an example. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • How is a p-type semiconductor formed? Explain with an example. [U] / [CO1] Ans. A p-type semiconductor is formed by doping an intrinsic semiconductor with trivalent impurity atoms, which create holes as the majority charge carriers. These impurities (acceptors) accept electrons and leave behind holes in the valence band. For example, doping silicon with boron (B) produces a p-type semiconductor. Formation (doping with trivalent/acceptor impurity, holes as majority carriers) – 1 mark Example (e.g., Si doped with boron) – 1 mark

questions.solution_html: • State the expression for the effective density of states in the conduction bandedge? [U] / [CO1] Ans. Correct expression for 𝑁𝑐– 1.5 mark Identification of terms (effective mass, temperature dependence, constants) – 0.5 mark

questions.question: What is the basic principle of light emission in an LED? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • What is the basic principle of light emission in an LED? [K] / [CO2] Ans. A light-emitting diode (LED) is a pn junction diode fabricated from a direct bandgap semiconductor such as GaAs, in which electron–hole recombination results in the emission of light. The energy of the emitted photon is approximately equal to the bandgap energy, ℎ𝜈 ≈ 𝐸𝑔. The basic principle of light emission in an LED is electroluminescence, where electrons and holes recombine in a forward-biased pn junction. This recombination releases energy in the form of photons with energy approximately equal to the bandgap. (The injected electrons recombine with holes in the depletion region and the nearby neutral p-region, known as the active region, producing light through injection electroluminescence.) Principle (electroluminesce nce / recombination of electron–hole pairs) – 1 mark Outcome (photon emission ≈ bandgap energy) – 1 mark

questions.question: What is the role of phosphor in white LEDs? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • What is the role of phosphor in white LEDs? [U] / [CO3] Ans. In white LEDs, the phosphor absorbs high-energy (blue or UV) light from the LED chip and re-emits lower-energy light (typically yellow) through photoluminescence. The combination of the original blue light and the emitted yellow light produces white light. Function of phosphor (absorption and re-emission / photoluminescen ce) – 2 mark

• Describe diffusion capacitance and its importance in forward bias operation [U] / [CO1] Ans Page No. 230, Optoelectronics & Photonics, Principles & Practices, Second Edition by S O Kasap Diffusion capacitance arises in a forward-biased pn junction due to the storage of excess minority carriers in the neutral regions. This capacitance affects the switching speed of the device, making it important in high-frequency applications.

questions.question: Compare the internal and external quantum efficiency of an LED / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the internal and external quantum efficiency of an LED [K] / [CO2] Ans Internal quantum efficiency is the ratio of the number of photons generated inside the LED to the number of electron–hole recombinations, indicating how efficiently carriers produce light. External quantum efficiency is the ratio of the number of photons emitted from the LED to the number of injected electrons, and it is lower due to optical losses such as reflection and absorption within the device. Hence, internal efficiency relates to generation, while external efficiency includes both generation and extraction of light.
  • - Definition of internal quantum efficiency – 2 marks
  • -Definition of external quantum efficiency – 2 marks
  • - Clear distinction (generation vs extraction losses) – 1 mark

questions.question: Explain the absorption in direct and indirect band gap materials / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the absorption in direct and indirect band gap materials [U] / [CO3] Ans In direct bandgap semiconductors, photon absorption excites an electron directly from the valence band to the conduction band without change in momentum, leading to strong and efficient absorption. In indirect bandgap semiconductors, absorption requires the assistance of a phonon to conserve momentum, making the process less probable and weaker. Hence, direct materials have a sharp absorption edge, while indirect materials show gradual absorption near the bandgap.
  • -Diagram-1 marks
  • -Explanation of direct bandgap absorption – 2 marks
  • -Explanation of indirect bandgap absorption (phonon involvement) – 2 marks

[U] / [CO3] Ans A multijunction tandem solar cell consists of two or more semiconductor layers with different bandgaps stacked together to utilize a wider range of the solar spectrum. The first cell is made from a wider bandgap material and absorbs photons with ℎ𝜈 > 𝐸𝑔1, while the second cell absorbs photons that pass through the first layer with ℎ𝜈 > 𝐸𝑔2. This layered absorption significantly enhances the overall efficiency compared to single-junction solar cells.
